archetypes.name: api-contract
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether every with_transient_retry call site in the plan matches the actual lib-net.sh API: argument order, _WTR_OUT/exhaustion semantics, fail-file contract, and the suspicious same-assignment symmetry in create-pr.sh
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every proposed with_transient_retry call in the plan against the actual lib-net.sh API contract: the first argument must be the predicate name, the second must be the fail-file path, and the command occupies the third-plus positions — flag any inversion or omission. For create-pr.sh, the plan assigns pr_json from _WTR_OUT in both the success and else branches; determine whether this is an intentional design choice (both paths legitimately consume captured stdout) or a copy-paste plan defect where the else branch should instead fall through to the conflict-text URL fallback without trusting _WTR_OUT from a failed call. For merge-pr.sh, verify that _WTR_OUT is guaranteed to be empty (not undefined or set to a prior value) on retry exhaustion, because the empty-on-exhaustion contract is load-bearing for refresh_pr_info and refresh_ci_state. For all three call sites, confirm that the plan's mktemp-plus-rm-f fail-file pattern is consistent with what the function actually appends to on final failure, and that transient_envelope_predicate_none returning 1 unconditionally does not silently suppress net-sig matching when a real predicate was intended. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-strictness
archetypes.rationale: Verifies that each with_transient_retry call shape is safe under the exact set -euo pipefail or set -uo pipefail mode of its target file, covering abort risk before fallback, local/mktemp set -u cleanliness, and Bash 3.2 portability of new constructs
archetypes.prompt_body: For each site where the plan introduces with_transient_retry, determine the exact shell strictness mode of the containing file (set -euo pipefail vs set -uo pipefail) and verify that the call form used—bare command, if-conditional, or assignment—will not trigger a set -e abort before any required fallback path executes; pay particular attention to create-pr.sh's recover_existing_pr_after_create_conflict path, where a bare non-zero exit under set -euo pipefail would silently skip the conflict-text URL fallback. Examine every new local declaration and mktemp invocation for set -u exposure: local without an initializer leaves the variable unset if the right-hand side is absent, and referencing it later under set -u is a fatal error. Check all new constructs—array syntax, parameter expansions, printf patterns—against Bash 3.2 compatibility requirements, since the plan does not explicitly confirm the new harness scripts avoid Bash 4+ features. Confirm that the exhaustion contracts differ correctly across the three call sites: exit 3 for rebase-push.sh, fall-through for create-pr.sh, and empty-string-on-exhaustion for merge-pr.sh, and that the call shapes actually implement those contracts rather than inadvertently unifying them. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: wiring-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether the plan's Makefile shard assignment, agent-lint.toml exclusion block, .md sibling coverage, and .PHONY recipe format each match the repo's exact conventions, with special attention to the ambiguous "shard 14 or 16" defect where both named shards are already occupied
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every wiring artifact specified by the plan matches the exact conventions already established in this repository. For the Makefile shard: confirm whether shards 14, 15, and 16 are already occupied (shard 14 carries test-rebase-push-force-lease, shard 15 carries test-rebase-push-fork-mode, shard 16 carries test-rebase-push-keep-on-conflict per Makefile lines 95-99), and judge whether the plan's "shard 14 or 16" language is a plan defect requiring a concrete new shard number. For the agent-lint.toml exclusion block: compare the plan's described exclusion format against the existing pattern at lines 305-432 of agent-lint.toml — specifically whether the comment block explains Makefile-only reachability, whether entries appear one string per line inside the exclude array, and whether the grouping and comment placement match existing rebase-push or lib-net harness entries. For the .md sibling files: check whether the plan guarantees all four required fields seen in lib-net.md and test-lib-net.md — purpose prose, a Scope or coverage list, an Edit-in-sync rule, and an optional invocation block — for each new script the plan introduces. For the Makefile recipe: confirm the plan's recipe uses the exact harness-timer.sh wrapper form `bash scripts/harness-timer.sh $@ bash scripts/test-<name>.sh` and that the .PHONY registration appears on a .PHONY: line rather than embedded in the main shard line only. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
